name: Storita Connector
author: Storita

sections.description:
Storita Connector exposes safe, read‑only access to your WordPress database over the REST API.

Key features:
– Read‑only queries (SELECT only) with robust validation
– API key authentication (or admin users via WP login)
– Nginx/FastCGI friendly header handling (X-Storita-Key, legacy X-DF-Key, or Authorization)
– Built-in rate limiting (1200 requests per hour per API key by default) and a maximum of 1000 rows per query by default
– Optional table whitelisting (restrict access to specific tables/patterns)
– Excluded tables list (empty by default); passwords, login keys and other secrets are always protected
– Secret redaction: password hashes, WordPress auth keys and salts and the API key are removed from every query result
– Schema explorer and health status endpoints; reading error logs is opt-in and off by default
– Admin settings page with copy‑to‑clipboard helpers
– Google Analytics 4 Integration: Proxy requests to GA4 using the existing Google Site Kit connection (supports standard and real-time reports).

This plugin is designed for integrations and reporting tools that need controlled, secure, read-only database access.

Requires a Storita.ai account. The plugin connects your store to the Storita.ai service (https://storita.ai); without a Storita.ai account the data it exposes has no consumer and the plugin has no purpose.

External services

Storita.ai

This plugin connects your WordPress/WooCommerce store to Storita.ai (https://storita.ai), a store analytics and assistant service. Storita.ai uses the plugin to read your store data so it can answer questions and produce reports about your store.

When data is made available:
– Only after the site owner configures an API key in Settings -> Storita.
– Only in response to requests sent to your site’s REST endpoints under the storita/v1 namespace (the legacy df-db/v1 namespace is still answered), either by the Storita.ai service using the API key in the X-Storita-Key (or legacy X-DF-Key) or Authorization header, or by a logged-in administrator.
– Nothing is sent on activation, and nothing is sent until an administrator clicks Connect to Storita or Open Storita. The plugin does not track visitors.

When the plugin calls storita.ai (only after an administrator clicks):
– Connect to Storita and Open Storita send a POST request to https://storita.ai/api/wordpress-onboarding/begin with: the site URL, an installation (connection) ID, a transaction ID, the administrator’s WordPress user ID and registration date, the approved store profile (store name, administrator name and email, currency, timezone, locale, country and site URL), the consent version and the plugin version.
– To finish the same flow the plugin then calls https://storita.ai/api/wordpress-onboarding/complete and https://storita.ai/api/wordpress-onboarding/ack, sending only the transaction ID, a one-time verifier and the name of the installed key.
– During the flow Storita calls back this site’s storita/v1/onboarding/proof endpoint once to confirm the request came from this site’s administrator.

What data is made available:
– Store profile, products, orders and customers data.
– The database schema (schema explorer) and read-only SQL SELECT query results (POST /query). Queries are SELECT-only and validated; tables the site owner excludes are blocked; credential tables are always blocked; and password hashes, WordPress auth keys and salts and the API key are removed from every result.
– Google Analytics 4 data, proxied through your site’s existing Google Site Kit connection (see below).
– Runtime health information. Log data (/health/logs, /health/logs/tail: debug.log, WooCommerce logs, the PHP error log) is shared only if the site owner turns on “Allow Storita to read error logs” in Settings -> Storita (off by default). Logs may contain personal data.
– The public /status endpoint returns only ok and the time.

The admin Test Connection feature calls only the site’s own REST URL (its own address) and never leaves the site.

Storita.ai legal documents:
– Privacy Notice: https://storita.ai/legal/privacy-notice
– Terms (Data Processing Addendum): https://storita.ai/legal/data-processing-addendum
– Trust Center: https://storita.ai/legal/trust-center

Google Analytics Data API (via Google Site Kit)

Only if Google Site Kit is installed and connected to Google Analytics 4: when the Storita.ai service or an administrator calls /google-analytics/report or /google-analytics/realtime, the plugin forwards the requested report fields (metrics, dimensions, date ranges, filters, ordering and limits) to the Google Analytics Data API (analyticsdata.googleapis.com) using Site Kit’s existing Google connection and the Google Analytics property configured in Site Kit. Google returns aggregated analytics report data. Nothing is sent to Google unless such a request is made, and the plugin sends no visitor data of its own.

  • Google Terms of Service: https://policies.google.com/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Google Analytics Terms of Service: https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/terms/us/

Usage

Base URL: https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1

The legacy base URL https://your-site.example/wp-json/df-db/v1 is still supported.

Authenticate by sending one of the following headers:
– X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY
– X-DF-Key: YOUR_API_KEY (legacy)
– Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
– Authorization: DF-Key YOUR_API_KEY

If you are logged in as an administrator (manage_options), endpoints are accessible without the API key.

Endpoints

1) POST /query
– Body params:
– query (string) – SQL SELECT query to execute
– query_base64 (string, optional) – Base64-encoded SQL (alternative to query)

Example (JSON body):
curl -X POST "https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1/query" \
-H "X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"query": "SELECT ID, post_title FROM wp_posts WHERE post_status=\"publish\" LIMIT 5"}'

2) GET /schema
– Query param: table (optional) – returns structure for a specific table; omit to list all tables

Examples:
curl -H "X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" "https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1/schema"
curl -H "X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" "https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1/schema?table=wp_posts"

3) GET /status
– Public health endpoint; no auth required

`

curl “https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1/status”
`

4) POST /google-analytics/report
– Queries Google Analytics 4 using Site Kit authentication.
– Body params: GA4 RunReportRequest JSON (metrics, dimensions, dateRanges, etc.)

Example:
curl -X POST "https://your-site.example/wp-json/storita/v1/google-analytics/report" \
-H "X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"dateRanges": [{"startDate": "30daysAgo", "endDate": "today"}], "metrics": [{"name": "activeUsers"}]}'

5) GET /health/logs and /health/logs/tail
– Off by default; enable “Allow Storita to read error logs” in Settings → Storita.

Security Controls

  • Requests per window – Rate limit per API key or IP (default 1200 requests per 3600 seconds).
  • Rate limit window (seconds) – How long the window lasts.
  • Maximum rows per query – Adds LIMIT automatically when missing; blocks excessive LIMITs (default 1000; 0 disables).
  • Excluded tables – Select specific tables to block. Nothing is blocked by default; passwords, login keys, API key secrets and 2FA secrets are always protected.
  • Allowed tables (optional) – Whitelist tables/patterns (e.g., wp_posts, wp_%). Leave empty to allow all tables unless excluded.
  • Allow Storita to read error logs – off by default.

Filters

  • storita_wp_rest_api_query – Filter the final SQL before execution.
    • Params: string $query, WP_REST_Request $request
  • storita_wp_rest_api_validate_key – Custom validation strategy for API keys.
    • Params: ?bool $is_valid, string $provided_key, ?WP_REST_Request $request
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings → Storita.
  4. Configure an API key and (optionally) security controls like rate limits and table whitelist.
sections.faq:
1) Does this plugin allow INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE?
– No. Only SELECT queries are permitted. Dangerous commands are blocked.

2) My server drops Authorization headers. What can I do?
– Send X-Storita-Key: YOUR_API_KEY (or the legacy X-DF-Key) or configure your server to pass Authorization headers. The plugin also inspects common server variables and getallheaders() when available.

3) How do I prevent huge responses?
– Use the admin setting “Maximum rows per query” (default 1000 rows). The plugin will append a LIMIT if missing and reject LIMIT values above the maximum.

4) Can I restrict which tables can be queried?
– Yes. You can exclude tables via “Excluded tables” and/or whitelist via “Allowed tables”. For the whitelist, provide exact names (e.g., wp_posts) or wildcard-like patterns (e.g., wp_%).

5) Does the plugin send data without my knowledge?
– No. Nothing is sent on activation. The plugin calls storita.ai only when an administrator clicks Connect to Storita or Open Storita, and then sends only the fields listed under External services. Store data is made available only in answer to requests from the Storita.ai service authenticated with your API key, or from a logged-in administrator.

6) Does Open Storita log Storita into my WordPress?
– No — it signs the WordPress administrator into their own Storita account; it never creates or changes a WordPress session.

7) Who can call the endpoints?
– Only the API key holder or a logged-in administrator. The /status endpoint is public and returns only ok and the time.

8) Can the SQL endpoint modify my database?
– No. Queries are SELECT only, validated, subject to row limits, and excluded tables are blocked.

9) Can the Storita service read passwords or secret keys?
– The plugin is designed to keep them out of reach. Credential tables are always blocked, UNION and derived-table queries on the users, user meta and options tables are refused, and password hashes, WordPress auth keys and salts and the plugin’s API key are removed from every query result. These are layered safeguards on a read-only SQL interface, not a guarantee against every possible query, so treat the API key like a password: share it only with Storita, and regenerate it in Settings → Storita if you disconnect.
sections.changelog:
2.3.5

  • Security fix: Storita REST responses (/df-db/ and /storita/, including errors) are never cached by page caches (LiteSpeed, Varnish and others), so cached keyed responses can no longer be replayed to visitors without a key.
  • On activation and after an update, purges only the plugin’s own REST URLs from LiteSpeed, WP Rocket and W3 Total Cache (never a full purge).
  • Adds an Open Storita button on the Settings page and an Open Storita link in the admin bar (administrators only, when connected).
  • The readme now discloses exactly when the plugin contacts storita.ai (only after an administrator clicks Connect to Storita or Open Storita) and what it sends.
  • Requests from non-administrators are refused with a 403 error.
  • No more false “API Key Not Configured” notice on sites connected through one-click onboarding.

2.3.4

  • After activation, takes you straight to Storita > Connect (single activation only; not bulk, network-wide or WP-CLI).
  • Adds a dismissible “Connect to Storita” admin notice while the site is not connected.
  • Includes 2.3.3: one-click switch from the old Storita WP plugin, a Replace manual key action, and uninstall cleanup of onboarding settings.

2.3.3

  • Adds a one-click switch from the old manually installed Storita WP plugin; your API key and settings are kept and backed up.
  • Adds a Replace manual key action so one-click Connect works after updating from the old manual-key plugin; uninstall now removes onboarding settings.

2.3.2

  • New: consent-first one-click connect to Storita from wp-admin; store settings are read automatically and only name and email are asked.
  • New: a connected site shows an Open Storita page without signup wording or re-consent.
  • Changed: the connect step retries once on transient connection errors.
  • Fixed: site-profile queries with WooCommerce HPOS; the manual API key fallback is kept.

2.3.1

  • Security: WooCommerce Analytics reports are served without switching to or acting as any WordPress user; the API key grants read-only report access only.
  • Changed: the read-only database and old-copy notices appear only on the Plugins screen and the Storita settings screen.

2.3.0

  • Added: optional read-only database connection for /query and /schema (constants STORITA_WP_RO_DB_USER and STORITA_WP_RO_DB_PASSWORD) with a 20-second session statement cap; falls back to the main connection with an admin notice.
  • Added: named API keys managed with WP-CLI (wp storita key add|list|revoke); the existing key keeps working as “default”.
  • Changed: rate limiting is counted per API key name; HTTP 429 responses carry a Retry-After header.
  • Changed: /query responses include truncated: true when the row cap cut the result.

2.2.4

  • Security: query results are scanned and password hashes, WordPress auth keys and salts and the API key are removed; UNION and derived-table queries on the users, user meta and options tables are refused.
  • Changed: rate limiting (1200 requests per hour per API key) and a 1000-row cap are on by default; sites still at the old 0 default move to the new defaults on upgrade. Each query has a 15-second MySQL time cap.
  • Changed: reading error logs is opt-in (Settings → Storita → “Allow Storita to read error logs”) and off by default.
  • Changed: the REST namespace is now storita/v1 and the X-Storita-Key header is accepted; df-db/v1 and X-DF-Key keep working.
  • Changed: the Google Analytics proxy always uses the property configured in Site Kit and forwards only GA4 report fields.
  • Changed: plugin slug and text domain are now storita-connector (main file storita-connector.php). Requires WordPress 6.2 or later.
  • Fixed: escaping in the admin connection-test results; notices no longer hide other plugins’ notices or appear site-wide; Clear Cache no longer flushes the whole object cache; all database queries use prepared statements.
  • Removed: the unused limit and offset parameters of POST /query.

2.2.3

  • Changed: nothing is excluded by default; the excluded-tables list is now empty unless you choose tables.
  • Added: WooCommerce API key, webhook and Wordfence 2FA secret tables are always blocked.
  • Upgrade: an untouched 2.2.2 default list is cleared automatically; customised lists are kept.

2.2.2

  • Prepared for the WordPress.org plugin directory: updates are now delivered by WordPress.org.
  • Removed the built-in update checker and the Check for Updates button.
  • Plugin name is now Storita Connector.

2.2.1

  • Fix: Site Kit GA proxy (/google-analytics/report, /google-analytics/realtime) returned HTTP 500 “Site Kit integration class not found” due to a namespace mismatch; corrected caller references so the Google Analytics fallback path works.

2.2.0

  • New endpoint: /df-db/v1/health/runtime — PHP/WP/WC runtime profile + Site Health results
  • New endpoint: /df-db/v1/health/logs — list available log sources
  • New endpoint: /df-db/v1/health/logs/tail — bounded log tail (allowlist + hard caps)

2.1.41

  • Fix: expose plugin version under meta.plugin_version on the auth-gated /site-profile endpoint so Storita’s backend can read it without the public /status disclosure (F-L-01).

2.1.40

  • Fix: DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TABLES now resolves against actual $wpdb->prefix at runtime; default exclusions work correctly on custom-prefix installs. MySQL system schemas (information_schema, mysql, performance_schema, sys) blocked by default.

2.1.39

  • Polish: remove debug logging, console statements, and dead comments; harden non-critical SQL calls; deduplicate auth helpers; add LICENSE file; correct readme branding; remove version disclosure from public status.

2.1.38

  • Security: redact SQL details from /query error responses; deny-by-default for analytics sub-endpoints; require manage_options for browser-based analytics access.

2.1.37

  • Security: filter sensitive rows/columns from /query results (wp_users password hashes, wp_options auth keys, wp_usermeta session tokens); reject queries that reference protected fields; block information_schema reconnaissance; move update secret to per-site option with wp-config override.
